result:
None of the three solutions matches the result I recall, and I am working from memory of the source paper rather than a derivation.

The recalled result is that, for large |t|, the N-th rational solution has N(N−1)/2 poles in the upper half-plane of x. Under the assumption of N real roots, the N solitons separate along the real line, so each pair of solitons accounts for one pole, giving C(N,2) = N(N−1)/2.

A check at N=1 supports this. A single algebraic soliton is a regular solution with no poles in the upper half-plane, so the count should be 0 there.

- **Solutions 1 and 3** give N, which gives 1 at N=1. That contradicts the regularity of a single algebraic soliton. Their claim that each soliton contributes its own pole is unjustified. (Both also print a garbled "Final answer", a function object instead of an expression.)
- **Solution 2** gives N(N+1)/2, which also gives 1 at N=1, so it is wrong too.

CHOICE: NONE
